findings.correction: “Anyway, get up. Another hour will do.” / “An hour?” / “Yeah. An hour.” / “I already told you. Even if we hurry, it would take two hours.” / “Exactly. An hour.” / It didn’t matter whether it took two hours or four. We were getting there in an hour, no matter what.
findings.current: “Anyway, get up. We only have one hour left.” / “Half an hour?” / “I said one hour.” / “You told us it would take at least two hours even if we hurried.” / “Exactly. One hour.” / It didn’t matter whether it took one hour or two. / We were getting there in half an hour, no matter what.
findings.defect: Earlier 한 시진 is two hours and 반 시진 one hour, but this beat treats 반 시진 as half an hour and 한/두 시진 as one/two hours, and Hyuk’s 말씀드렸잖아요 becomes “You told us.”
findings.rationale: The joke is Taekyung halving Hyuk’s 한 시진 estimate. Hyuk reminds Taekyung of Hyuk’s own estimate; the narrator then dismisses even 한/두 시진 and insists on 반 시진. The draft both reverses the speaker of the estimate and collapses the converted units, so the punchline numbers no longer match.
findings.source: “반 시진만 더 가면 된다.” / “반 시진이요?” / “응, 반 시진.” / “말씀드렸잖아요. 최대한 빨리 가도 한 시진이라니까요.” / “그러니까. 반 시진.” / 한 시진이든 두 시진이든 상관없다. / 무조건 반 시진 안에 간다.

findings.correction: The squad leader collapsed at the most important moment, and these damn squad members haven’t even offered to carry him in my place, whether I drop dead or not.
findings.current: The squad leader collapsed at the most important moment, while these damn squad members haven’t even offered to carry me if I die.
findings.defect: 대신 업다 is taking over the piggyback of the unconscious squad leader, not offering to carry Hyuk.
findings.rationale: Hyuk is already carrying Jin Taekyung. 대신 업겠다는 is an offer to piggyback that burden instead of him. Making Hyuk the load reverses the complaint.
findings.source: 조장이라는 인간은 정작 중요할 때 픽 쓰러지고. 조원이라는 새끼들은 내가 죽든 말든 대신 업겠다는 소리도 안 하고.

findings.correction: It had been a time when that embarrassing character, chivalry, had still felt enormous.
findings.current: It had been a time when the character for chivalry had seemed enormous.
findings.defect: 낯간지러운 is omitted, so the Head Elder’s embarrassed/self-conscious stance toward 협 is lost.
findings.rationale: The source marks 협 as an awkward, almost cringeworthy word that nonetheless felt large. Dropping 낯간지러운 flattens that characterization.
findings.source: 협(俠)이라는 낯간지러운 글자가 크게 느껴지던 시절이었다.

findings.correction: His judgment had been clouded by rage over losing his son and by impatience with the situation.
findings.current: His judgment had been clouded by grief over his son and impatience with the situation.
findings.defect: 분노 is rage/anger at his son’s death, not grief.
findings.rationale: The Korean names two causes: anger at the loss and haste about the war. Grief is a different emotion and softens the motive for the rash march.
findings.source: 아들을 잃은 분노와 상황에 대한 조급함에 판단력이 흐려졌다.

findings.correction: “So, Mujin.” / I gave Hyuk Mujin’s choked-up face a good-natured smile. / “Get up. Now.”
findings.current: I smiled warmly at Hyuk Mujin’s flushed expression. / “So, Mujin.” / I smiled even wider. / “Get up.”
findings.defect: 울컥한 is a choked-up surge of feeling, not flushed; 당장 is dropped; a second smile is inserted here that belongs to the later 더더욱 환하게 beat, and the remaining smile is moved before the address.
findings.rationale: Source order is address, then one amiable smile at an emotional expression, then an immediate get-up command. The draft changes the emotion, adds a grin, and spends the later brighter smile early.
findings.source: “그러니까 무진아.” / 나는 울컥한 표정의 혁무진에게 사람 좋게 웃어 보였다. / “당장 일어나.”

summary: Critical subject/quantity errors in the 시진 bargaining joke and in who would be carried; plus lost 협 self-consciousness, 분노 rendered as grief, and a displaced smile/emotion beat.
